utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'm sorry for the delay which was due to a technical problem obviously. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we proceed I would like to make sure that the two accused are able to follow what is being said in the courtroom in a language they understand. Mr. Milan Lukic, do you understand what is being said?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we cannot hear the accused. THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic. THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we then proceed to the representation. Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Dermot Groome; I'm accompanied by Steven Cole, Francesca Mazzocco, Maxine Marcus, and Sebastiaan van Hooydonk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence, Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: You need your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise. Jason Alarid on behalf of Mr. Milan Lukic and also accompanied by Mihailo Lakcevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. And the case is now that you have been formally appointed counsel, lead counsel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was informed by Mr. Petrov today that it should have been in my e-mail between the Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: We will in all respects treat you as lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am Djuro Cepic. Appearing with me, Ms. Christina Kerll as our legal assistant and Mr. Jens Dieckmann as a co-counsel in our Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, the purpose of this Status Conference is to review where we are. We met three months, I believe, to the day last time when we had the last Status Conference. In the meantime the very able Ms. Yvonne Featherstone, the Senior Legal Officer, have conducted three 65 ter conferences in order to move things along and there has been a -- I won't say a flurry, but there has been a lot of submissions on both sides relating to matters of disclosure, alibi, and to the pre-trial briefs. And obviously things are at this point looking much, much brighter than it did three months ago. And the aim of this Status Conference is to lay down some dates for the trial to actually start, the Pre-Trial Conference date which we previously assumed was, as you know, the 16th of May, a day which came and went. No formal notice from the Bench of the change and you all know that matters both relating to the parties but also to administrative parties inside the Tribunal made it impossible to have that date as a Pre-Trial Conference date. So now we're looking at other options and we'll come back to that. I will run through the list of open issues as I see them and as I have been informed that we have. Before I go into that, I will first note that we had a filing officially this morning from the Prosecution relating to a wish to have the indictment amended. I was given a courtesy copy of it yesterday, so I wasn't totally unaware. And the response date for that expires the 26th of June, which is the normal date. And I will certainly not pre-judge where the Trial Bench will as a decision address the motion and the eventual responses. However, I would with you, Mr. Groome, like to inquire as to the timing of this amendment; and I do that because normally, as we all know, we are looking -- it's now rather to reducing the scope of an indictment at this stage of a pre-trial phase and not to expand it. I read the motions. You do not have to give me all that's in it, but I would like to address the question whether that the fact that new charges are brought in I believe to both of the accused and also some other substantial changes, for instance, to the concept of joint criminal enterprise. My question is simply this, Mr. Groome: Whether the basis for these wishes to amend the indictment, if they are based on facts that were known to you or facts that have recently come to light.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as explained in the motion, when I first took over this case end -- middle of December, it was around the same time that both accused notified the Court and the Prosecution that they would rely on alibi evidence. Now, of course when -- just last week that alibi evidence has been perfected with respect to Sredoje Lukic and we still have very vague details about it with respect to Milan Lukic. But with the information that we did receive, began a process of examining in our evidentiary collection what if any statements or evidence existed that could shed light on the issue of whether or not they were present during the times they committed these crimes. And in doing that, Your Honour, it seemed that more than a few of the statements that were taken in some cases over a decade ago, put the -- both accused at different -- in Visegrad at the time that they now say that they were not there. Most remarkably or most notably is one woman who says she was brutally raped by Milan Lukic, just hours before -- three times just hours before the Bikavac fire. So in fulfilling my obligations to present evidence relevant to alibi I will have to call this witness and she will be examined by me about the circumstances of these rapes, she will be cross-examined by the Defence, and the Court at the end of the case will be called upon to assess her reliability, her credibility, and will necessarily have to make a determination whether or not on the day of the Bikavac fire Milan Lukic raped her three times. Now, it seems to me in fairness to this woman and other woman like her who will be called to similarly testify, that having put herself through the retraumatisation of having to go through these events, in many cases when these women initially gave their statements, they expressed their refusal to testify because it was such a painful event in their lives. Some had since married and they had never told their husbands or their children about these events and here I was sending investigators to knock on their doors explaining the situation and asking would they come forward. Some agreed, some expressed some reluctance, some asked for time to discuss it with their families. But of the women that now are willing to come forward and to talk about these events, it seems to me that they have the right to have the Court adjudicate whether or not a crime was perpetrated against them because their evidence has now necessarily been implicated by the alibi defence. And it is in the course of investigating the alibi defence, Your Honour, that this evidence came into focus and was formulated into the indictment that was -- or the proposed indictment that was filed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: You were, Mr. Groome, if I understood it reminded of these facts by the notice of alibi given by the accused; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, although it's more than reminded. They were never part of the indictment but it's when they came to light.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I'm just trying to clarify the fact you had it, it was old, but you were reminded because of new information from the other side?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: As I said I will not go any deeper into this. There's no point to have counsel for the accused address this at this point. The Chamber will obviously render a decision whether to grant or deny this request for amendment in due course and certainly well before we get into any Pre-Trial Conference. So I intend to move on to open questions of another nature. We have been exercising quite a bit with the notices of alibi. The Chamber issued a decision on the 26th of May this year whereby notice and information should be provided to -- from the accused to the Prosecution, and the Defence for Sredoje Lukic did that, I believe, on the 2nd of June this year. And we are still, I believe, waiting for the Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic to, A, provide notice to the Court; and B, provide material to the Prosecution. So where are we on this, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, we did tender the initial information to the Prosecution and I apologise to the Court for not putting it into a formal pleading for yourself, but by the due date earlier rendered by the Court we tendered what we had in total. And so as a matter of fact we're trying to facilitate interviews as we speak of the alibi witnesses that we do have. We've been since tendered several names by the client and just defence preparation meetings and we are just beginning the investigative state. Some of them may qualify as alibi, but we have not determined and I don't want to misrepresent to the Court the nature of the testimony that may come since they may cover a wide spectrum of issues relevant to the defence but not necessarily qualitative of a Rule 67 disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. Well, in order to assist and facilitate the Chamber we'd be grateful for having the lacking notice not later than a week from now, which I think you could provide us with, unless you could do it today, but certainly not later than a week today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'll tender it by Monday, Judge. I leave on Tuesday and I think there's no problem getting that done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I hope the response will be the same for the next dead-line and that is to notify the Prosecution of the witnesses that are for you to -- under the label of alibi to follow your obligation and here the time I have in mind for you to do that is the end of the month, i.e., the 30th of June, so not later than the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think with the initial investigation we're moving from today, I hope that's feasible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I hope it's more than feasible, I hope it reaches us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. We then have -- there are some other matters concerning the Defence alibis which I think was satisfactorily dealt with during the 65 ter conference and are expected to be dealt with also by the parties outside the courtroom so I won't spend any time on it but move to the question of the clarification of the Defence pre-trial briefs. Here there have been two decisions by the Bench, one on the 29th of May and the second on the 9th of June this year with a request and a new dead-line which was actually yesterday. And I'm happy to note that Sredoje Lukic file was expected yesterday, but we are still waiting for the Defence of Milan Lukic to do the same. Comments, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. To comply with the Trial Chamber's decision on that, it was really impractical considering I was flying across the 10th to the 11th, but more importantly, Your Honour, that some of the clarifications that are requested really require a deeper understanding of the facts and I don't want to misrepresent myself to the Court and basically give information that down the road turns out not to be credible or justified. We're just getting our office set up right now. We've got a team in movement, and I'd like the opportunity to clarify, I think that's important, but I don't want to do it from a position of lack of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. That's very commendable, and that's why I'm minded to give you a week more than I gave the Defence for Mr. Sredoje Lukic. That means that you are to comply with this not later than the 18th of June. I think that should be feasible. Moving on then to other matters where the responsibility rests more with the Chamber than with the parties, we have the Prosecution motions for -- regarding 92 bis, ter, and quater statements. That is ready for decision and that decision within due course be taken by the Trial Chamber. The same goes for Rule 94, i.e., adjudicated facts and notices as to agreed facts, the Prosecution motion and notices, and we will be able to address that unless parties indicate that discussions on these matters are ongoing, but I understood that from the Prosecution's point of view at least, and that squares with the Defence of Sredoje Lukic, this is not a priority, i.e., to pursue the avenue of try to get more agreed facts. Is that a correct understanding, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know that Mr. Cepic has had a meeting with a member of my staff and it was a productive meeting. It hasn't reached any finality, but as I said at the earlier conference today the Prosecution is available whenever counsel from either team is in town to discuss the matter further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dieckmann will raise our position about that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dieckmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As we explained and -- I think in the last 65 ter conference we are definitely willing and able to negotiate about agreed and adjudicated facts. The problem is that we are still preparing -- conducting interviews of the Prosecution and they have some practical problems, but we are very confident that we could solve it together with the Prosecution. And this is all we can say in the moment. If we have conducted or finished our investigation, we could sit together and start substantial negotiations, we are willing to do this, but this is from today everything we could say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dieckmann. Well, I encourage obviously both parties to do their utmost in order to reach anything that could diminish the need for live testimony in this case. The third matter under this headline is the motion regarding protective measures applications number 4 and 5 and other submissions in relation to that and to the witness list. And I expect to be able to have a decision from the Chamber next week on these issues to clarify those matters. I believe we have a list of some 20 witnesses which are affected by this in various ways. So that will be dealt with next -- not later than next week. There is also an outstanding Rule 54 bis motion from Sredoje Lukic, and since this is technically a confidential matter my idea was not to go into the substance of it. I just check whether it is, as has been indicated, the intention of the Sredoje Lukic Defence to wait for whatever comes out from requests and then perhaps refile the application. What can you tell me about this, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we requested again that material from broadcasting companies in Bosnia, and I received the answer from one of companies and they replied to me that they are agreeable to deliver us that material but just with the order of Trial Chamber. So we have to file that motion as soon as we receive the second answer from another broadcasting company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. Well, we'll look forward for your application. There are, I understand, questions relating to matters of disclosure which have been -- which are not dealt with in the motions and others that I have discussed now that parties are engaged in discussions. Are there any particular issues that the parties need to raise here? I'm looking, obviously, to the Defence first. Is there anything you need to raise or can I assume that the matter that was discussed during the 65 ter conference will be pursued and if there is a need to involve the Chamber on any of these issues you will do so. Is that correct, Mr. Alarid?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. If we have some new requests we will raise that by e-mails directly to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Groome, I think there are matters of -- concerning some witnesses that also may change the position and affect the present witness list. Any comments on that, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, if you could maybe clarify what point you're asking me to address.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, first of all, I should have asked whether you have any comments on what the counsel said now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to disclosure, no, Your Honour, there are no issues the Prosecution wants to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I was then quickly moving to a slightly different matter, namely that I understand there has been some change on your part with regard to witnesses put forward by you that may need some decision. Would you care to comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, could I ask that we go into closed session for this purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We then with those matters dealt with are ready to focus on readiness for the trial. And my assessment is that if we can have compliance with the dead-lines already laid down and also taken into account the discussions that I believe have been had regarding conflict of other trials and also travel problems and the like. It seems that it would be possible, unless you strongly object, to have a Pre-Trial Conference in this trial on Wednesday, the 2nd of July this year. I take comfort in the fact that no one is protesting. Ah, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, at the 65 ter conference this morning I indicated that the week of the 2nd I have a couple trials set back home that need to be resolved so they're not bothering us in a month. And if I can resolve that, I am available the next week, preferably the latter part of the week, but technically the whole week if I had to make arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Alarid, we understand that there may be other pressing assignments that makes things problematic. We are certainly not going to try to make the impossible. I mean, if you are due somewhere else, you are due somewhere else. On the other hand, there is now some time between here and then and maybe things in the other end could change and evolve so you could accommodate and actually be here for the Pre-Trial Conference on the 2nd of July. Or are you stating that that is totally impossible? That was a leading question, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It is. Yes, it is, Judge, and the reason being it may be small matters in the grand scheme of things but they are pending trials that have been waiting a long time as well and by resolving them I free myself up I think to accommodate the accelerated trial-prep situation much better. If I can get those finalised, that's two less things that are going to interfere I think with the more important time, which is complying with preparation issues for the Court. And also I think with having a little more time to assess the situation, it may make the Pre-Trial Conference a little more fruitful, as a week sometimes can make a difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: How are things on your end, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be acceptable to the Prosecution. When I say acceptable, Your Honour, I mean the 2nd of July that you mentioned and any date after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No problem with us. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I'm minded at this stage, Mr. Alarid, given the fact that so many are involved, to say that for now the 2nd of July is standing; however, we would be prepared and I would appreciate if you could then when we get closer -- we now work with the 2nd of July as a Pre-Trial Conference, and in the hope that things may, despite your assessment at this moment, clear in the US end, if I can put it that way, we would be prepared to work out another date, and that date would then be the 9th of July, which is a week after. But we all now put our hope in the fact that also Mr. Alarid should be able to make the 2nd of July, but we are prepared to take the 9th as an alternative. That would, on the other hand, mean, since the idea was to use the 9th not only for opening statements but also to start the evidence, the 9th of July would be a very heavy day. But we're all used to heavy days in the Tribunal, so I think that could be accomplished. By that I have disclosed that if we now were to have the Pre-Trial Conference not on the 2nd, which there is a risk for, the 9th would start with the Pre-Trial Conference, to be followed by opening statements, and if the time permit, obviously, the first lead of evidence. Because the fact that the trial starts would not mean that we will go full steam all the way to recess because we understand that on both sides there may be a need to additionally clarify points, but I think it's important, not the least for the accused who have been waiting, to see that the trial actually formally starts. So the idea is to have the remainder of that week, i.e., the 10th and 11th of July, for the Prosecution case to start. And then there will be a break, that is the plan at the moment, and then the case will be resumed after the normal opening of business of the Tribunal. Have the parties understood the thinking behind this scheme of things? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I understand the scheme of things, although I think I've made our position pretty clear in submissions over the last couple of weeks regarding our really competence to proceed in that rapid a manner. I think that it's difficult to assess our preparedness at this stage just because we're just really putting the team together and we're really getting to the meat and bones of this case and it would be an extreme prejudice and disadvantage and that is why it was important for me to advise Mr. Lukic of those issues and that's why we signed the waiver of the speedy trial portion of the rule in our last submission, is because it is important, although they've been waiting, it's more important I think to have a competent defence presented. And if we're doing all our preparation while the OTP is starting their case, that really places us in a risky proposition for providing a competent defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. I'm aware that you are -- consider yourself to be a latecomer to the case; however, if I recall correctly, you have now been appointed to the Defence for now quite some time, in March I believe. And there comes a time when things just need to be ready, and I think it would not compromise your client's interests if you made all efforts on your part to try to abide by the times now laid down. I think the Chamber has been reasonably understanding with your hitherto failure to comply with those time-lines that have been laid down. I am aware that you have asked for extended time and so on, but you're also aware of that you have not been able to comply with the times that we have laid down before. So I can only urge you to try to do your utmost in this respect. And this is also then linked to the fact that obviously the Prosecution, if the hearing of witnesses after the opening of the Prosecution case is to start - which I hope it will be on the 9th of July - there is a need for you, Mr. Groome, to inform counsel for the two accused of what witnesses you intend to start with. Are you ready to say when you could give notice of your witnesses that you start to lead?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Featherstone raised that issue this morning. Actually, you have several copies of the first 16 witnesses and I will provide those after the conference to all the parties in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I think that's very helpful and that I think should make life somewhat easier for you, Mr. Alarid, in the preparation of the case. Mr. Cepic, do you have any comments on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. Actually, we are ready of course for this trial. We have been preparing more than two years, but according to second amended indictment. So any changes in the indictment causing huge problems for us, especially in relation to mode of responsibility because we have been preparing our defence, as I said, for more than two years. Now just a couple days or weeks before the trial commencement, we've been receiving some proposal which is completely different than all our preparation, which changes everything, everything. We have to start from the zero if it would be accepted. That is the first problem. And we would be grateful just to know the agenda for July because my learned friend, Mr. Dieckmann, will be busy in Germany. So I'll be present here, so just to know how many witnesses is planned for July and how many working days because I do have also final activities in the Milutinovic et al. case, 8th of July is the dead-line for the final brief and last week of July is the schedule for the closing arguments. It is so important for me because it means last activities in that case where I spent more than 25 months. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. I am fully aware, as are others, of your other commitments at this Tribunal. And as I -- let me first address your concern with the motion for amending the indictment, and I'm certain that what you just said now will be reflected also in the response, and obviously the Chamber will give due weight to the motion and to reply and try to come with a judicious decision in due course. As to your second, I had understood it that the Prosecution are now providing the first line of witnesses obviously need to perhaps indicate what the Prosecution indicates to be able to cover during the three days in July that we're talking about, the 9th, the 10th, and the 11th. And that's the end, that's the total of what this case will take as far as scheduling for July. So I think that answered your second question, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So just to let me summarize, we are at the moment working despite the dissatisfaction of Mr. Alarid, and I hope that can be resolved, with the Pre-Trial Conference on the 2nd of July. If it turns out - and I'm sure that Mr. Alarid when we get closer will inform us that that is totally impossible because of his other commitments, the Pre-Trial Conference will be held early on the 9th of July, which is also the date for the opening statements by the Prosecution and for the Prosecution to start to lead its witnesses, and which those witnesses are the parties will be informed I believe already after the close of this Status Conference. And then the case will continue on the 10th and the 11th of July, and after that there will be a break for the parties to be able to draw breath, review, and then continue after the recess. Has that been fully understood by all? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, it's understood, Judge, but your -- one of the issues that I have is that I know in some instances opening is waived until a later date. My fear -- and I just don't believe in that as a trial attorney. I think it's very important for the Defence to set the stage at the outset because otherwise, in a vacuum it leaves the Prosecution's case as the only explanation of the events from the very beginning and then if we wait until the beginning of the Defence case to make our opening, it's sort of like rebuttal and I think that's a poor way to start a case. And so my position is I think it would be very difficult, given the time constraints of myself, to actually be prepared to give a formal opening statement on the 9th under any set of circumstances, much less having our pre-trial that morning and then starting. I think that's a very difficult task to make with our accessibility to the actual meat and bones of this case at this juncture. And that's why I was hoping that absent anything else, those three days could be put out until when we were really thinking about resuming the trial, which is of course August after the summer recess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. We have noted what you have said, Mr. Alarid, and that's what could be said at this time. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just one thing, if I may ask, I kindly ask OTP to have at least ten days prior to the commencement of the trial tentative witness notification for July month just to have enough time to be prepared, because as I said, I have too many activities in another case and to be ready for the trial commencement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. I was under the impression that the Prosecution would not have any problems to comply with that. Is that correct, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will provide that. One thing I would note, the third witness when I distribute it people will see is a very substantial witness. I think given the schedule that the Chamber is talking about it might be wise to postpone that witness until after the break. So with that amendment I will be providing that information. With respect to delayed disclosure, Your Honour, I think some of the terms require 30 days before trial. We're now less than 30 days, but within the next day or two we'll meet our obligation as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. That would seem to be satisfactory. Thank you. With that I think, unless the parties wish to raise any other matter that has not been raised so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Nothing at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just to inform this honourable Trial Chamber that the last week OTP conducted interview with Defence alibi witnesses in Belgrade, they interviewed three witnesses. That's all. Nothing more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic. We have noted that. That brings me to the penultimate issue, and that is to make sure that the two accused do not have anything that they wish to raise in front of the Chamber. Mr. Milan Lukic, is there anything that you wish to raise? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Nothing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic. THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Nothing to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, this from my perspective brings this Status Conference to a close and we'll now stand adjourned.
